considered_but_rejected.why_not_added: SPRINT MINESUP-E made an explicit, documented decision (see engine.ts comment above FUZZY_STOPWORDS, 'Volontairement PAS ajoutés') to KEEP 'science'/'technology' as legitimate specialty-differentiator words for higher-education institution names, with a real cited example (avoiding conflating 'Higher Institute of Science and Technology' generically). FUZZY_STOPWORDS is shared across ALL registries (MINESEC/MINESUP/MINSANTE/future ministries) — adding 'sciences' globally would silently override that prior, deliberately-scoped decision for every other registry, not just MINSANTE health-training names, which is exactly the kind of blind domain-term stopword addition §6/§7 of this sprint's brief prohibits ('never add a distinctive domain/program term blindly').

null_geography_semantics_fix.problem: Before this sprint, geo comparison used `normalizeGeo(region) || normalizeGeo(city)` — REGION always took priority over city via `||` short-circuit, so `city` was structurally NEVER consulted whenever `region` was non-empty (true for all 22 pilot rows, region='Ouest'). This meant two schools in different cities within the same region always looked 'geographically consistent by default', and — separately — a genuine NULL/NULL city pair never counted as a false positive match ONLY because it fell back to comparing region (which is a legitimate, if coarser, signal, not a NULL/NULL artifact).
null_geography_semantics_fix.fix: Replaced with `geoAgreement(regionA, cityA, regionB, regionB)` (exported from engine.ts): compares CITY first if both known (most specific), falls back to REGION only if city is unknown on either side, and returns 'UNKNOWN' (never a positive match) if neither is known on both sides. Generic — applies to every registry (MINESEC/MINESUP/MINSANTE/future), not MINSANTE-specific.
null_geography_semantics_fix.regression_tests: scripts/school-registry/lib/matching/__tests__/matching-minsante-g1.test.ts §7.C (geoAgreement(null,null,null,null) === 'UNKNOWN'; region-only fallback verified separately as 'MATCH', never conflated with the NULL/NULL case) and §7.D (explicit city conflict tests).
